title.narrative: Hands Off Botswana

description.narrative:
Brief overall description: To reduce violence against sex workers, Aidsfonds works together with Sisonke (sex worker-led organisation from Gaborone and BONELA (a national NGO). Paralegals will continue to support sex workers in accessing legal services. At safe spaces in four districts sex workers can access support groups, receive psychosocial support and health services. Human rights violations against sex workers will be documented and used for lobbying and advocacy purposes. The organisations will advocate for policy and service provision changes at district level, as well as during high level meetings. Relationships with key stakeholders, such as service providers, community and religious leaders and police officers will be sought or intensified to reduce stigma and discrimination.
Main objectives and outcomes: Hands Off II partners work to reduce violence against sex workers at community, national and regional level. Outcomes BONELA and Sisonke work on mainly include: an empowered and resilient sex worker movement demands its rights; increased access to and use of inclusive services for sex workers; and a more enabling and supportive environment for sex work.
Description of target groups: The programme’s primary target group is female, male and transgender sex workers, meaning those who receive money or goods in exchange for sexual services, either regularly or occasionally. INERELA+ will also work with lawyers, government officials, policymakers and service providers.
Additional information: Sex work in Botswana is conducted in a wide range of locations: from outdoor and street based sex work to restaurants, truck stops, bars, hotels, private homes or hostels. With the closing down of mines the locations where sex work takes place continue to move. There are an estimated 6.700 sex workers in Botswana. Due to the illegal status of sex work, sex workers experience difficulties in accessing health, social services and in seeking justice and legal compensation.

comment.narrative: There has been an improvement on the performance as comapred to the January- June report, as a result of intesified monitoring visits and support group sessions

They were reached through support groups. Though sex workers were reached, the way numbers were documented did not warrant for them to be reported, as they were not disaggregated by age and gender, thus they were not included in the report. Plans have been put in place that during the review meeting, a day shall be set aside to refresh the paralegals on data collection and reporting tools and good data quality. Acceleration plans have been put in place to ensure that the target is met. Efforts are made to reach more in the remaining months

comment.narrative: The performance for this year is low compared to the previous year for reasons that some of the sex workers have migrated to places where there is lucrative business such as Maun and Ghanzi, where they opened new mines. Most of the foreign sex workers have gone back to their countries. Staff turn over has also affected meeting targets, as new paralegals had to be orientated on the project. Efforts have been put in place to accelerate implementation for the remaining period to ensure that annual targets are met. There has been an increase in the number of male sex workers reached, this is as a result of collaborating with other stakeholders during their men campaigns.

title.narrative: Number of human rights violations reported to the police

description.narrative: Number of human rights violations reported to the police

comment.narrative: Sex workers are encouraged to report cases, though most of the foreign sex workers are reluctant to report for fear of being deported. Child and Gender units have been established in police stations where clients who have been violated can report their cases in privacy. However, there is much that needs to be done in terms of sensitising the police on human rights. Selibe Phikwe has reported high number of clients who reported cases to the police, and this is as a result of a mutual relationship between the paralegal and the police, as there are instances whereby when the police conduct outreaches, they invite the paralegal along to disseminate messages and the paralegal can also invite the police to outreaches. In some instances mediation is done between the two parties, therefore there wont be any need to report to police.

Sex workers are untrusting of the police officers so some cases go unreported. But advocacy at the DMSAC level has been leveraged, unfortunately, the police focal persons arent always present. We will partner with GBV focal persons in the Police department as an entry point to link sex workers cases.
There were reports, however, police officers still do not sign referal slips which we can use to prove that indeed the sex workers have accessed the services

comment.narrative: Sex workers were referred for counselling services with other service providers providing mental and psyschosocial health services such as BGBVC, Government social workers, Silence Kills and police, as a temporary measure while Sisonke is still finalising the parameters of the agreement contract with the identified service provider. It is hoped that with the engagement of a psychologist, more sex workers who have been reluctant to access services from public health services will come forth.

There is a need, however mental health issues are still mystified in Botswana. SWs would go for 1 session and would not continue with the services. Efforts are being explored as how best to get SWs consistently attend sessions.

title.narrative: Long term outcome 2.1

description.narrative: Sex workers use community led prevention, care and health services

title.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing community-led support after violence

description.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing community-led support after violence

comment.narrative: There has been a decline in the number of sex workers in need of community led support after violence. It has been noted that some of the cases which could have been assisted particularly with emergency fund, only presented their need for support when they had recovered. Some of them particularly the non-citizens without valid documents were reluctant to report cases due to fear of deportation following revelation of illegal residence.

Were given medication and nutritional support. There are several to the underperformance of this indicator.a)some cases were submitted, however, they were not meeting the set requirement criteria for one to be supported with emergency fund, b) other cases were reported and submitted late to the review committee such that by the time they are reviewed, they are overtaken by events in that the situation is no longer emergency warranting the need for the support. BONELA and Sisonke, will be address the challenge of the selection criteria and timeframe for submission of requests during the review meeting, taking in to consideration, the context of what's happening on the ground d) a lot of requests were made during the lock down and as result of movement restrictions during COVID as most sex workers could not continue with the normal business, and this increased the number of those in need of support

title.narrative: Long term outcome 2.2

description.narrative: Sex workers use rights based tailored health services

title.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing health & testing (if applicable) services

description.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing health & testing (if applicable) services

comment.narrative: Clients were referred and linked to different services such as ART refills, initiation on ART, re-initiation for those who defaulted on ART, TB and STI screening, HTC, initiation on PrEP. It was noted during the data verification process that most of the clients who have been referred for services had not yet returned the completed referral slips. It was therefore difficult to ascertain if they have received services or not. Some of the sex workers, reported to have gone access the services but did not take the referral slips along for fear of being stigmatised by service providers. BONELA proposes for accompanied referral which is escroting the clients to services providers and hopefully this will will improve linkage to health care services.

The second half of the year in Botswana is a very mobile season for sex workers particularly that the second half of the year is a holiday season. We also loose clients when we have referred them for services as lines are usually long, this meaning that they are lost to follow up when they do not return the refferal slips.

description.narrative: Stigma and discrimination against sex workers is reduced

title.narrative: Number of community leaders trained on the rights of sex workers

description.narrative: Number of community leaders trained on the rights of sex workers

comment.narrative: Community leaders such as tribal and religious leaders, VDC members. BONERELA has been engaged to sensitise community leaders on the rights of sex workers, however this has been on ad hoc basis. There is need to intensify/ make the relationship/engagement official such that BONERELA is engaged on regular basis.

The National AIDS and health promotions agency has been supporting BONELA and Sisonke to scale up the sesitisatons of community leaders to end stigma as they are the gate keepers of community perceptions, this has led to a positive outlook of sex workers by religious and traditional leaders.

The reason is that there was no financial support to facilitate the trainings. However, paralegals would visit them at their respective areas of work and have dialogues with them. One thing we have realised late was that the paralegals were having dialogues with community leaders but they were not documenting, which made verification difficult.
